why: Spotify track IDs (22 base62 chars), YouTube video IDs (11 chars), and Vimeo clip IDs (numeric, 7-10+ digits) are opaque and impossible to recall reliably. Never write an ID from memory or pattern-completion. Past runs produced 4/7 dead Spotify IDs and 1/10 dead YouTube IDs because the ID looked plausibly real but was hallucinated.
video_note: Video on a Data2Story page may be EITHER (a) a verified oEmbed embed — YouTube or Vimeo — where the platform player carries the license and you re-host nothing, OR (b) best-effort, a CC-licensed clip fetched from Wikimedia Commons / Openverse and passed through the Scout license+identity gate. Prefer an embed for rights-encumbered footage; only re-host a clip whose license is on the allowlist.

workflow.name: Source it from a real page
workflow.detail: Not from prior knowledge. Use WebFetch against a Spotify search page, an artist/album page, the YouTube watch page, the Vimeo clip page, or a credible third-party listing. Copy the ID out of the actual HTML/URL you fetched. If you cannot retrieve a real page that contains the ID, do not invent one — drop the instance.

workflow.name: Verify with oEmbed before writing
workflow.detail: Run the matching command in Bash and confirm a 200 plus a sensible title. The oEmbed path is the single source of truth for an embed's validity: it must (a) return HTTP 200 AND (b) parse as JSON with a non-empty `title`. Treat any non-200, any non-JSON body, OR an empty/garbage title as a FAIL and drop the instance — never write an embed you could not parse. YouTube and Vimeo both accept the plain watch/clip URL (no manual ID extraction needed); Spotify needs the track/album/playlist URL. Use the *-json status helpers below: they fold the HTTP-200 check, the JSON-parse check, and the title sanity check into one command so a silent failure cannot slip through.

commands.robust_oembed_any: For any provider: first run the *_status command (must print 200), THEN run the matching *_title command (must print a non-empty, sensible title that parses as JSON). Pass ONLY if both hold. Substitute the provider endpoint from the `endpoints` map above into <full-oembed-endpoint-URL>.

interpret.200: embeddable. Set verified: true and copy the returned title into verified_title.
interpret.404: the ID does not exist. Drop this instance entirely — do not guess again with a similar ID.
interpret.403: the video exists but the uploader disabled embedding (common for major-label music videos and brand ads). Drop the instance and find an alternative (an official VEVO upload, an artist's own / Vimeo channel, or a different illustrative clip).
interpret.401: Vimeo: the owner restricted embedding to specific domains (domain-level privacy). Drop the instance and find a publicly embeddable clip.
interpret.non_json_or_empty_title: Even on a 200, if the body does not parse as JSON or the title is empty, treat it as a FAIL — the player will not render reliably. Drop the instance.

workflow.name: Title sanity check
workflow.detail: Compare verified_title against your label. If they refer to clearly different content (different song, artist, film), this is a wrong-ID hit — drop the instance and re-search. Do not paper over the mismatch by editing label to match the wrong track.

workflow.name: Never write an unverified embed
workflow.detail: If verification fails or you skipped it, omit the instance. A blog with 3 working embeds is far better than one with 7 where 4 show 'video unavailable'.
